jobs.description:
Job Description

Are you passionate about IT, business, and finance? As a Senior Business Consultant, you will specialize in banking and investment, collaborating with clients and experienced colleagues to design IT solutions and develop expertise in investment processes and corporate actions.

Netcompany Banking Services

We deliver various IT solutions and services to banks and savings institutions across Denmark and other Nordic countries. We provide a modern, cloud-based core banking platform serving more than 50 Nordic banks with over 2 million end customers. Our solutions encompass daily banking operations, mobile and internet banking, payments, investment management, risk management, compliance, and open banking.

Responsibilities

We are looking for a Senior Business Consultant with an interest in digitalization and financial services to support initiatives within banking and investment. You will contribute to analyzing business needs, mapping processes, and designing IT solutions in close collaboration with clients and colleagues.

You will join a team of highly experienced professionals, where you will contribute with your established domain expertise, while continuously expanding your knowledge of IT solutions within banking and investment. As a part of the emerging team in Aarhus, you will become a go-to within banking and investment solutions.

Your responsibilities will typically include:

• 
Analyzing clients' business needs and translating and formulating requirements into IT solutions within the banking and investment domain.

• 
Mapping business processes and facilitating workshops with clients to identify needs, challenges, and opportunities for optimization.

• 
Co-leading the analysis and design of solutions related to investment processes.

• 
Collaborating with colleagues and clients on solution design, testing, refinement, and implementation, while supporting user involvement, training, and change management.

• 
Acting as a Subject Matter Expert, leveraging in-depth domain knowledge to drive project outcomes, provide expert guidance, and facilitate knowledge sharing across teams.

About you

You actively seek understanding by asking questions and encourage learning through curiosity and dialogue. You enjoy understanding how business processes work and how IT can support and improve them. Deadlines do not intimidate you, and you are willing to go the extra mile when needed. To succeed in this role, you:

• 
Have extensive experience within the banking sector and especially the investment domain, ideally working at the intersection of IT, business, and organization.

• 
Hold a relevant master's degree, such as Cand.merc. IT, Cand.it., or a similar degree with a focus on the intersection of finance and IT.

• 
Have a genuine interest in IT and digitalization, preferably combined with an interest in finance, banking, investment, or financial services.

• 
Have comprehensive experience with investment-related processes. Previous experience within banking or investment is a requirement.

• 
Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritize an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

We are looking for a Financial Controller to lead the operational and analytical work behind our monthly close, group consolidation, project controlling and control environment of a fast-growing energy trading and technology group – and to rebuild them AI-first, so our numbers are faster, more reliable and ready for scale.

Why this role matters

Hybrid Greentech is scaling fast as a VPP, BRP and electricity retailer across Denmark, and Northern Europe. Energy trading means large and volatile daily revenue, cost and cash transactions – so quality , accuracy and liquidity control are not back-office topics; they decide how fast we can grow. This role exists to give management, the board and investors numbers they can trust, on time, and to build controls and automation that scale with the business rather than with headcount. The same discipline is needed in our consultancy arm, where technical consultants deliver advisory and EPC management projects: clear project economics, timely invoicing and early warning when a project drifts.

The role

As Financial Controller, you report to our Finance Manager and work closely with the CFO and our accountant in a small, hands-on finance team. You lead the operational and analytical work within the financial steering, reporting and finance and business analytics; running the month-end close, the consolidation of our group entities in Denmark and abroad, balance sheet reconciliations, project controlling and the day-to-day operation of our internal controls. This is an individual contributor role with high ownership and direct visibility towards management.

You will work in close collaboration with our settlement team, project managers and business owners to ensure adequate financial steering and reporting, partner with our accountant on more complex accounting topics, and work across trading, portfolio management, commercial and engineering. We are a tech-first company with high AI adoption, and we expect you to work that way too: AI tools, scripting and automation are your default approach to removing manual work from close, reconciliation and reporting – combined with the judgement to know when a number needs a human review.

**What you will do

**

• Lead and execute the monthly close and group consolidation, including account mapping, intercompany eliminations, reconciliations and variance analysis, and prepare the monthly financial and business review for the CFO, management and the board.

• Set up and run project controlling – project budgets, hours and utilisation, work in progress, milestone and fixed-fee revenue recognition and timely invoicing – giving project managers and business owners clear steering on margin, estimate-to-complete and cash.

• Automate and rebuild our reporting flow – from ERP trial balances to consolidated P&L, balance sheet and cash flow – using AI tools, scripting and data pipelines, replacing manual spreadsheet steps with controlled, repeatable and documented processes.

• Operate and strengthen our internal controls within the framework set by the Finance Manager, including segregation of duties, payment and bank authorisations and documented business procedures, and drive follow-up on auditor recommendations.

• In close collaboration with Settlement, ensure trading-related balances – settlement, imbalance costs, customer prepayments and deposits, and collateral posted to TSOs, DSOs and exchanges – are correctly recognized, invoiced and reconciled

• Support cash and liquidity forecasting and management with the Finance Manager and CFO, including rolling cash forecasts, collateral and trading risk capital tracking, and early warning on cash exposure.

• Prepare and analyse the annual budget and monthly forecast updates for the Finance Manager and CFO, maintaining our driver-based budget model and following up on budget-versus-actual deviations with business owners.

• Handle key accounting areas such as revenue recognition and accruals, capitalisation of development projects, grant periodisation and month-end cost accruals, collaborating with our accountant on more complex accounting topics.

• Support in the year-end close and audit for all group entities, including annual reports, tax specifications and intercompany agreements, in close collaboration with Finance Manager and our external auditors.

• Work closely with our Settlement team and business owners to ensure adequate financial steering and reporting – turning data into insight on gross profit by revenue stream, cost of execution and unit economics, and building dashboards that let the business self-serve.

**

What you bring**

_Experience and skills (Required)

_

• 5+ years of experience as a controller, in audit or in a group finance role, ideally in a multi-entity set-up.

• A relevant degree in accounting, finance or economics (e.g. cand.merc., HD-R or cand.merc.aud.).

• Proven hands-on experience running month-end close, consolidation and year-end audit under the Danish Financial Statements Act (Årsregnskabsloven)

• Hands-on experience with ERP systems, preferably e-conomic

• Solid understanding of balance sheet accounting, revenue recognition, capitalised development costs, accruals and intercompany transactions.

• Experience with project controlling – budgets, work in progress, utilisation and project margin follow-up – ideally in a consultancy, engineering, Trading or EPC business.

• A genuine AI-first way of working: you use AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot daily and can show concrete examples of finance processes you have automated (e.g. with Python, SQL, Power Query, APIs or low-code tools).

• Strong Excel and financial modelling skills combined with a structured, control-minded approach and high attention to detail.

• The ability to work independently in a fast-paced scale-up, prioritise under pressure and explain financial matters clearly to non-finance colleagues.

• Language: English (required); Danish

_Nice to have

_

• Experience from energy trading, utilities, commodities or financial services – e.g. settlement, collateral, imbalance or margin processes.

• Experience with e-conomic, time registration or PSA tools, ERP migration to a more scalable platform, and BI tools such as Power BI.

• Experience with public grant-funded projects, transfer pricing or building internal controls in a growth company.

• A background from a Big 4 or mid-tier audit firm.

**What we offer

**

• Real responsibility: the chance to improve how close, controls and reporting are run in a scaling energy trading group – not just maintain them.

• An AI-first workplace where you get the tools and the mandate to automate, experiment and rethink how finance is done, working closely with our CFO, trading and tech teams with exposure to board and investor reporting.

• Competitive compensation and performance-based incentives.

• A collaborative environment with short decision lines, high trust, and strong cross-functional execution.

• The opportunity to work with forward-looking customers and partners driving electrification and the green transition in Northern Europe.

Ready to apply?

Ready to build an AI-first finance function for a company where every megawatt-hour traded must be settled, reconciled and controlled? If you combine accounting rigour with a builder's mindset, we would love to hear from you.

Deadline

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis until 10 December. We reserve the right to close this vacancy earlier if a suitable candidate is identified and accepted.

Do you want to head up quality and food safety at Harboe’s production site in Skælskør? Do you possess a strong professional background within QA/QC, and are you motivated by driving a proactive quality culture in close collaboration with production? Then you might be the one we are looking for.

About us

Harboes Bryggeri produces and sells beer, soft drinks, and malt- and fruit-based ingredients and beverages. Production takes place at our breweries in Skælskør and at the fully owned Darguner Brauerei in Germany. Both sites produce and package beverages in glass, cans, and PET, while Dargun also handles draught beer. Malt-based ingredients and concentrates are produced in Skælskør.

Quality and food safety are fundamental to everything we do. The Quality Department plays a key role in ensuring compliance, maintaining high standards, and safeguarding product quality from raw material to finished goods.

The position and Key responsibilities

As Quality Manager, you will have overall responsibility for leading Harboe’s Quality Department and ensuring the effective operation, maintenance, and continuous alignment of our quality management system.

You will become a part of the Group Quality Team and report directly to the Plant Director in Skælskør, with a dotted line reference to the Director, R&D, ESG and Quality.

Your primary focus will be to lead and develop our QA and QC teams while ensuring that our quality and food safety standards are consistently implemented and maintained across the organisation. Through visible leadership and close collaboration with production and other key stakeholders, you will ensure that quality remains an integral part of daily operations.

Building on our existing quality management system, you will drive systematic and continuous quality improvements. The role covers in-house products, ingredients, raw materials, packaging materials, and quality-related activities throughout production. You will ensure compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements while ensuring that the quality function supports customer expectations and operational needs.

Main focus areas include:

• Leading and developing the Quality Department, including QA and QC teams, ensuring clear priorities, strong collaboration, and a high level of engagement.

• Ensuring effective implementation and maintenance of the quality management system (IPW), including compliance with standards such as IFS and FSSC 22000.

• Planning, conducting, and following up on internal and external audits, including training of the internal audit team in Skælskør.

• Maintaining close cooperation with production, including handling of deviations, root cause analysis, and follow-up on corrective actions.

• Ensuring professional handling of customer complaints, including documentation, investigation, and timely follow-up.

jobs.occupation: Experienced Software Developer – Team Box Collab
jobs.description:
Build software at scale. Influence how we build it. Help modernize a product area at the heart of construction projects.

Dalux is growing, and we are looking for an experienced software developer to join our Box Collab team.

You will build software in our File Management product (Box) that enables communication and collaboration across construction stakeholders—for example, file comments, sharing, versioning, and review. This domain is widely used and deeply integrated across the Dalux product suite, so reliability, performance, and strong technical design are essential. In Box Collab, we foster an engaging, enjoyable work environment where people take ownership and accountability for outcomes. You’ll join a young, skilled team with strong opportunities to influence both product evolution and architectural direction.

**Your role

**As an Experienced Software Developer, you will take ownership of complex product and technical problems from idea to production.

You will join a full-stack development team working closely with a Product Manager and Product Designer. We expect experienced developers to contribute beyond their individual tasks: helping make good technical decisions, improving the codebase and architecture, sharing knowledge, and raising the engineering standard around them.

Within Box Collab, there is a particular focus on strengthening and evolving the technical foundation of the product while continuing to deliver new functionality.

Your work can include:

• Owning complex features and technical problems end-to-end

• Designing and implementing scalable, maintainable solutions

• Contributing to architectural decisions and the technical direction of Box Collab.

• Improving the structure of an established codebase and reducing technical debt

• Helping evolve boundaries and modularity within the application

• Sparring with and mentoring other developers

• Working closely with Product Management and Design to understand problems and find the right solutions

• Bringing new ideas, technologies, and development practices into the team when they create real value

We expect experienced developers to have opinions, challenge existing solutions, and be comfortable having their own ideas challenged in return.

**AI-assisted software development

**We are significantly increasing our focus on AI-assisted development across Dalux.

We are actively exploring how AI can improve the software development lifecycle – from understanding requirements and exploring technical approaches to coding, testing, review, debugging, refactoring, and automation.

The Box Collab team is already experimenting with how these tools can improve its day-to-day development work.

As an experienced developer, we want you to take an active role in that development: experimenting with new workflows, critically evaluating their value, sharing what works, and helping establish good engineering practices around AI-assisted development.

Practical experience using AI as part of your development workflow is an advantage. More importantly, you should be curious about how these tools are changing software engineering and willing to continue evolving your own way of working.

**Technologies we work with

**Box Collab is a full-stack product area primarily built with:

• C# / .NET

• Angular / TypeScript

• MSSQL

• Elasticsearch

Our wider platform runs on a distributed cloud architecture using AWS.

Experience with our exact technology stack is useful, but strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to understand and improve complex systems matter more.

**What would make you a particularly strong match?

**We are looking for an experienced software developer with strong technical fundamentals and the ability to influence the software around you.

For this particular team, we would especially value:

• Str ong professional experience with C# and .NET

• Strong DB management experience, including indexing strategies and query performance optimization.

• Experience improving or modernizing established software systems

• An understanding of Domain-Driven Design, modular architecture, or similar approaches to structuring complex applications

• Experience mentoring or providing technical sparring to other developers

• Practical experience with AI-assisted development tools and workflows

You do not need to match every point.

Technical judgment, curiosity, and the ability to make an established product better are more important than having worked with exactly the same technologies or architectural patterns before.

**Product development at Dalux

**Our product teams bring developers, Product Managers, and Product Designers together.

Developers are expected to understand the problem being solved and contribute to finding the solution – not simply implement specifications handed to them.

As an experienced developer, you will have an important voice in balancing user value, usability, technical feasibility, business viability, and long-term technical health.

Our products are relied upon by professionals worldwide, making performance, stability, maintainability, and quality important parts of everyday engineering.

**What You Can Expect From Dalux

**Dalux is a software company at heart.

As an experienced developer, you can expect:

• Significant ownership of the software you build

• Real influence on technical solutions and engineering practices

• Skilled colleagues who enjoy technical discussion and constructive challenge

• Close collaboration between Engineering, Product Management, and Design

• Short paths from technical ideas to decisions and implementation

• Opportunities to improve an established product and architecture

• A healthy work-life balance, with a strong focus on a sustainable work week and no overwork culture.

• Clear opportunities for professional and career growth.

• An environment actively investing in AI-assisted software development

• High levels of trust and freedom in how you solve problems

• A social workplace with monthly events and employee-driven clubs

All Dalux software development takes place in-house at our headquarters in Vibenshuset, Copenhagen. Working together in person is an important part of how we collaborate, share knowledge, and make decisions quickly.

**About Dalux

**Dalux is a Danish software company founded in 2005 by Bent Dalgaard and Torben Dalgaard.

We build digital tools that make the construction industry smarter and more efficient. Using our own 3D BIM technology, Dalux develops user-friendly software used in more than 140 countries worldwide.

Our core technology is developed entirely in-house, giving our developers the opportunity to influence both the products and the technology behind them.

**Interested?

**If you are looking for a role where you can remain hands-on while gaining greater technical influence and helping evolve an established product and architecture, we would like to hear from you.

We recruit continuously as Dalux grows.

**Application deadline:

**Ongoing

_Are you motivated by becoming the technical expert behind products and solutions that support clean water and energy? Do you thrive in a role where you connect technical development, business needs, and customer requirements? Are you excited by the opportunity to influence products throughout their entire lifecycle while collaborating with stakeholders across the organization?

**Here Is What The Job Entails

**In the role as our next Technical Product Specialist within our software applications, your job will be to provide technical expertise across the product lifecycle while ensuring that products, solutions, and technical documentation remain accurate, compliant, and competitive.

More specifically you will be:

• Acting as the technical liaison between Research and Development, Sales, Customer Service, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders

• Providing technical support including tender support, sales support, product training, and advanced troubleshooting

• Serving as the technical expert on products, configurations, software solutions, and applications

• Maintaining technical product information and documentation

• Supporting product lifecycle activities including new product development, maintenance, and phase in and phase out activities

You will experience the freedom to act and leave your mark on how we manage and support our products throughout their lifecycle. Therefore, you will work closely with technical and commercial stakeholders across the organization, gain deep insight into our products and technologies, and play a key role in ensuring knowledge sharing, product adoption, and continuous improvement.

**Meet your future team

**With direct reference to Senior Manager, Technical Product Management, you will become part of the technical product management team. As a team, we are committed to ensuring our products remain technically accurate, competitive, and capable of meeting both market and business requirements, and you will have a key role in achieving this. In the team you will experience close collaboration with colleagues across product management, development, customer service, sales, and supply chain. Together we support products throughout their lifecycle while ensuring strong stakeholder engagement and knowledge sharing across the organization.

Did you know? As a Technical Product Specialist, you will work with stakeholders from many different functions, making every day an opportunity to learn something new about our products, technologies, and customers.

**Less About Us, More About You

**We are looking for a Technical Product Specialist who is ready to take ownership of technical product activities and who is motivated by solving complex challenges. You achieve this through strong collaboration skills, technical curiosity, and a structured approach to your work.

In order to succeed, we imagine that you:

• Hold a degree in Engineering within Electronics, Software, Mechatronics, or a similar field.

• Have an understanding of product development, product lifecycle management, and technical product support

• Have experience with, or an understanding of, software-related systems such as Swagger documentation, Jira, Confluence or comparable platforms. A general end-to-end understanding of hardware and connectivity along with insights to APIsis an advantage.

• Demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving skills combined with the ability to communicate technical information clearly

• Have experience with product related systems such as Configure Price Quote, Product Lifecycle Management, Enterprise Resource Planning, or similar platforms.

We also value experience developing and delivering technical training and knowledge sharing activities

As we are an international organization it is important that you are fluent in English.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, you could still be a good candidate for the position. If you find the role intriguing, do not hesitate to apply.

**We are more than the ordinary workplace

**We cherish the good colleagueship which we all contribute to, the only limit is your engagement. As we are a big organization you are bound to find one or more colleagues who share the same interest as you. This might be in our board game club, cycle team, during our yearly summer festival or on the padel court. For example, is our Head of System Engineering and Information Technology Denmark also our volunteer padel instructor while our Software Test Engineer runs weekly spinning classes.

Besides the best colleagues you could imagine, we also offer:

• Work life balance through flexible working hours

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

**Do you want to be a part of Kamstrup?

The job will be located at Kamstrup's headquarters in Stilling, between Aarhus and Skanderborg.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Senior Manager, Technical Product Management, Kirsten Sahl, by phone: +45 89 93 10 00.

**Get to know us

**At Kamstrup, you'll become part of a close-knit community that genuinely cares about one another, fostering connections both in and out of the workplace. Our team comprises innovators, dreamers, and doers, united by an unyielding passion to challenge the status quo, find better solutions, and constantly push the boundaries of what's possible all with the purpose of securing clean water and energy to the maximum number of people. With an unwavering commitment to growth, we offer opportunities for you to leverage your skills and drive our business to new heights, empowering you to leave your mark on our future and grow with us. Are you an experienced SCADA engineer or technical service lead who wants to remain hands-on while taking responsibility for reliable service delivery? Would you like to combine solving technical problems with guiding colleagues and improving business-critical services supporting renewable energy?

As our new Service Manager Level 1 SCADA & Power Plant Control, you will be responsible for the reliable, secure and efficient delivery of agreed SCADA and Power Plant Control services supporting Vattenfall’s renewable-energy operations. Your scope includes WTG and substation SCADA, hybrid park controllers and interfaces to WTG Power Plant Controllers.

You will combine hands-on SCADA engineering and incident resolution with functional leadership of a dedicated service team of Level 1 SCADA and Power Plant Control engineers. Alongside your own technical assignments, you will prioritise the team’s work, coordinate suppliers and support functions, and drive continual improvement while meeting agreed service levels.

Working closely with customers, stakeholders and the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager, you will help develop standardised, proactive service delivery that combines effective incident response with preventive maintenance, lifecycle planning and long-term service improvement.

Be in your element with BA Wind

As part of BA Wind you will play a key role in one of the most exciting pipelines in the industry with 24GW of capacity stretching out more than a decade ahead across our key European markets.

You won’t only be involved in developing projects but pioneering cutting-edge innovation, new business models and ways of working with communities and the environment. Working as part of a leading European utility also means you could be helping a growing number of major businesses and brands achieve their own sustainability goals through partnerships.

Qualifications

Your role

You will take responsibility for the delivery and performance of the services within your agreed scope, from their introduction into operation through ongoing support, improvement and eventual replacement or retirement.

Your service scope covers Level 1 SCADA for WTGs and substations, together with assigned Power Plant Control systems and interfaces, including hybrid park controllers and interfaces to WTG Power Plant Controllers. You will take responsibility for their operational support, controlled changes, lifecycle management and continual improvement within agreed ownership boundaries.

This role combines hands-on senior SCADA engineering with functional service leadership and does not include personnel line management. You will personally undertake engineering work while coordinating and prioritising the service team’s activities, monitoring outcomes and making risks, dependencies and resource needs visible. Capability and capacity requirements will be aligned with the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager, with resources requested from the respective line managers.

You will apply your practical engineering expertise to diagnose faults, restore services and implement controlled technical changes within your agreed scope and authorisation. You will provide technical guidance to colleagues, assess operational risks and challenge proposed solutions, combining hands-on delivery with effective planning and coordination across organisational boundaries.

You will participate in the team’s on-call rotation, personally diagnosing and resolving incidents affecting SCADA and Power Plant Control services outside normal working hours, within your agreed technical scope and authorisation. You will involve other engineers, OEMs and suppliers when specialist support is required, follow agreed escalation arrangements and contribute to root-cause investigations and corrective and preventive actions.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Service scope and support arrangements: Maintaining clear service definitions, ownership boundaries, agreed service levels, support responsibilities and escalation arrangements, aligned with the agreed service mapping, the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager and customer expectations.

• Service delivery and hands-on engineering: Managing reliable, secure and efficient day-to-day delivery of SCADA and Power Plant Control services, including monitoring, incidents, service requests, problems, changes and lifecycle activities. Personally configuring, testing, commissioning, maintaining and improving assigned systems, controllers and interfaces within approved procedures and authorisations, while balancing engineering assignments with service-leadership responsibilities and agreed priorities.

• Service performance: Monitoring performance against agreed service-level agreements (SLAs), key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational targets. Reporting on service availability, incident response and restoration, recurring issues, risks and improvement actions.

• Incident response and problem management: Personally diagnosing and resolving incidents affecting assigned SCADA systems, Power Plant Control systems and interfaces, while coordinating additional engineers, OEMs, suppliers and support functions as required. Ensuring timely service restoration and clear stakeholder updates, investigating root causes and implementing or assigning corrective and preventive actions, with follow-up to completion.

• Backlog and delivery planning: Managing and prioritising the service team’s backlog, dependencies and delivery plans based on higher-level guidance, operational impact, risk and available capacity. Planning your own engineering assignments alongside service-leadership responsibilities, balancing urgent operational needs with planned maintenance, lifecycle work and improvements, and making capacity trade-offs visible.

• Capability and capacity planning: Identifying the skills and capacity required to deliver agreed services and roadmap commitments, aligning them with the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager, and requesting resources from the respective line managers and making the consequences of resource gaps visible.

• Lifecycle engineering and controlled change: Executing the agreed service roadmap through hands-on engineering and coordination of upgrades, migrations, patching, configuration changes and lifecycle replacements. Preparing, implementing or reviewing assigned changes, with appropriate risk assessment, testing, rollback arrangements, documentation and operational handover through approved processes.

• Supplier and stakeholder coordination: Coordinating contributions from suppliers, specialists and internal support functions, monitoring delivery against agreed responsibilities and service commitments, and following up on issues. Supporting technical and service-related purchasing or contract discussions with the responsible procurement and contract owners.

• Project requirements and transition to operations: Providing OT operations and maintenance requirements to projects whose deliverables will enter the service team’s scope. Agreeing operational acceptance criteria with the relevant stakeholders and participating in readiness reviews and handovers, checking support coverage, monitoring, documentation, recovery arrangements and unresolved risks.

• Operational documentation and knowledge: Producing and maintaining technical records, configuration information, operational runbooks and troubleshooting guidance for your own engineering work. Ensuring that the service team maintains relevant service and asset records, clear support responsibilities, escalation arrangements and accessible operational knowledge.

• Continual improvement and technical guidance: Using service-performance data and operational experience to identify, prioritise and implement improvements that reduce recurring incidents and strengthen reliability, efficiency and supportability. Standardising repeatable services and work packages, contributing to technical reviews, and supporting colleagues through practical guidance, knowledge sharing and appropriate automation.

• Security, compliance and audit support: Ensuring that applicable cybersecurity, regulatory and operational requirements are incorporated into service delivery and lifecycle planning, in collaboration with the responsible service engineers, cybersecurity and compliance functions. Coordinating relevant evidence and follow-up actions for audits and reviews.

• Risk management and escalation: Maintaining visibility of service risks, dependencies, delivery constraints and outstanding decisions. Escalating issues beyond the service team’s mandate or capacity to the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager and other responsible stakeholders, with clear recommendations and operational consequences.

Your profile / who are you?

You hold a relevant bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, automation or control engineering, computer engineering, industrial IT, systems engineering or a related discipline. Alternatively, you have developed equivalent professional competence through a relevant technical qualification and substantial hands-on experience in SCADA or industrial OT engineering and operational support.

You have several years of hands-on experience engineering, operating and supporting SCADA systems or comparable industrial OT solutions, including recent practical experience diagnosing faults, restoring services and implementing controlled changes. You can personally diagnose faults, restore services and implement controlled technical changes. You have also demonstrated the ability to coordinate technical work, prioritise operational needs and guide colleagues or suppliers. Your background may be as a senior engineer, technical lead or service manager who has remained technically active; a previous formal Service Manager title is not required.

You understand the demands of supporting business-critical systems and can translate operational needs into clear priorities, responsibilities and delivery plans. You are comfortable taking responsibility for service outcomes while working with engineers, suppliers and line managers in a matrix organisation.

You have excellent written and spoken English skills and can communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. The role may be subject to security clearance, and candidates must be able to meet the applicable screening requirements.

You bring knowledge and experience in:

• Operational service management: Applying structured incident, problem, service-request, change, configuration and lifecycle-management practices, with clear ownership, service levels and follow-up.

• Hands-on SCADA engineering: Practical experience configuring, integrating, testing, commissioning, maintaining, operating and supporting SCADA systems and interfaces, including documenting and validating technical changes.

• SCADA and OT environments: Understanding the role of SCADA in asset monitoring and control, including interfaces and dependencies between WTG and substation systems, power plant control, central control systems and supporting infrastructure. You can engage meaningfully with specialists and assess the operational implications of technical proposals.

• Service leadership and prioritisation: Coordinating multidisciplinary service teams and suppliers, managing backlogs and dependencies, identifying capacity requirements and resolving competing priorities within an agreed mandate.

• Operational resilience and secure engineering: Practical experience supporting service availability through monitoring, backup and recovery of SCADA applications and configurations, secure access, vulnerability handling and controlled technical changes, in collaboration with the teams responsible for supporting infrastructure.

• Service introduction and handover: Translating operations and maintenance needs into project requirements and acceptance criteria, assessing operational readiness and coordinating the transition of new or changed solutions into supported services.

• Supplier and stakeholder management: Establishing clear expectations, following up on service commitments, coordinating across organisational boundaries and handling escalations constructively.

• Incident and problem management: Diagnosing faults across SCADA applications, Power Plant Control systems, interfaces and connected systems, including dependencies on server services, networks, certificates and service accounts. Personally restoring services within your technical scope and authorisation, investigating root causes and implementing corrective and preventive actions, with specialist or supplier support where required.

• Performance analysis and improvement: Using service metrics, incident trends, risks and operational feedback to identify improvement priorities, track actions and communicate progress and results.

Additional experience that would be valuable:

• Experience with wind-turbine and substation SCADA platforms, hybrid park controllers, or OEM-specific WTG Power Plant Controllers and their interfaces.

• ITIL or comparable service-management training, or relevant OT cybersecurity training.

• Experience with service-management, backlog-planning, reporting and knowledge-management tools.

Personal traits

To succeed in this role, we believe that you:

• Take ownership of service outcomes and follow through on commitments, decisions and improvement actions.

jobs.occupation: Senior Project Engineers - Substations and Export Cables
jobs.description:
Business Area Wind is responsible for Vattenfall’s Onshore and Offshore Wind, as well as other non-hydro renewable initiatives like PV/Solar and batteries. We currently develop, construct and operate wind generation assets across Sweden, Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands and the UK.

As part of BA Wind you will play a key role in one of the most exciting pipelines in the industry with 24GW of capacity stretching out more than a decade ahead across our key European markets. You won’t only be involved in developing projects but pioneering cutting-edge innovation, new business models and ways of working with communities and the environment. Working as part of a leading European utility also means you could be helping a growing number of major businesses and brands achieve their own sustainability goals through partnerships.

We are looking for several Senior Project Engineers to strengthen our offshore transmission engineering capabilities within Business Area Wind, Offshore, Engineering.

We are seeking engineers with experience in one or more of the following areas:

• Offshore substations

• Onshore substations

• Offshore export cables

• Onshore export cables

We welcome engineers from all relevant disciplines across these scopes, with particular interest in HV and LV systems for onshore and offshore substations, and civil engineering for onshore substations and onshore export cable routes. Your assigned scope will reflect your background and experience.

You will take ownership of assigned engineering work packages, from FEED and tendering through delivery and handover.

In these roles, you will apply your experience to shape and challenge supplier solutions from the owner’s perspective, coordinate technical expertise and resolve delivery issues.

Within the project, you will report to the respective Package Manager and work autonomously within your assigned scope, drawing on technical specialists and collaborating with Interface Managers, Procurement and other project functions.

Your responsibilities:

• 
Deliver assigned engineering work packages in accordance with contractual requirements and project and contract milestones. Plan and coordinate activities, and monitor and report on safety, quality, progress and cost within your scope.

• 
Apply a systems engineering mindset so decisions within your scope support the performance, integration, optimisation and delivery of the overall transmission system—not individual contracts in isolation.

• 
Keep the design basis, requirements, interface decisions and contractual scope aligned, coordinating the impact of changes on affected packages.

• 
Work with Interface Managers and project teams to define and resolve technical and contractual interfaces, including scope boundaries, engineering inputs and delivery dependencies.

• 
Assess supplier proposals and technical decisions with safety as the highest, non-negotiable priority. Consider functionality, availability, quality, constructability and maintainability alongside CAPEX, OPEX, schedule and delivery risk.

• 
Coordinate technical specialist input and challenge unnecessary complexity and over-specification in supplier solutions.

• 
Identify and manage scope-related risks and opportunities, maintain an up-to-date risk and opportunity register, and coordinate mitigation. Keep technical positions, assumptions, deviations and residual risks visible throughout the project lifecycle.

• 
Support supplier qualification and technical evaluation. Incorporate Employer’s Requirements and specialist input into tender documentation, making scope boundaries and interface requirements clear. Assess bids, deviations and assumptions to support negotiations and award.

• 
Follow supplier engineering while respecting supplier design responsibility. Coordinate technical reviews, verify supplier documentation against contractual requirements, and resolve technical queries, deviations and changes with relevant stakeholders. Align technical decisions with the respective Technical Authority.

• 
Coordinate manufacturing or construction quality surveillance, inspections and acceptance testing, including FAT where applicable. Verify supplier documentation and technical completion, and support construction and commissioning teams in resolving technical issues and ensuring interface readiness. Verify as-built documentation and support taking-over, handover and close-out for safe, reliable and efficient operation and maintenance.

• 
Share lessons learned and contribute to improving requirements, engineering practices and project delivery.

We welcome applications from candidates at either Intermediate or Senior level. For Intermediate-level candidates, we are particularly interested in individuals who demonstrate strong technical capabilities, a high level of motivation, and a willingness to learn and develop further

Location: The role will be based in one of Vattenfall’s office locations in Kolding (Denmark), Amsterdam (Netherlands) or Hamburg (Germany). Some travel to other Vattenfall offices, project locations, supplier facilities and construction sites should be expected.

Qualifications

Your profile:

• B.Sc. or M.Sc. in electrical engineering, power engineering, structural engineering, civil engineering, mechanical engineering or another relevant engineering discipline.

• At least five years of relevant engineering experience, including responsibility for electrical, structural, civil or mechanical engineering work packages in the development or delivery of one or more of the following: onshore or offshore HV substations, subsea export cable systems or onshore HV cable systems. Owner-side experience is preferred.

• Experience in major project development or delivery, including technical oversight, interface coordination or acceptance of supplier work. Experience in multi-contract delivery, where the owner retains responsibility for integration across suppliers and packages, is preferred.

• Experience reviewing and challenging supplier and contractor engineering, including interfaces with other disciplines, fabrication, construction and installation.

• A systems engineering mindset, demonstrated by resolving interfaces between disciplines, suppliers and packages in the interests of the overall transmission system.

• Strong safety and engineering judgement, including the ability to distinguish essential requirements from unnecessary complexity.

• Commercial awareness of how technical choices affect CAPEX, OPEX, schedule, contractual risk and project delivery.

• Self-motivated and able to work autonomously, with good communication and influencing skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across disciplines and packages.

• Professional working proficiency in English.

jobs.occupation: Join us as a Student Data Engineer in Fund Accounting Products
jobs.description:
Would you like to put your studies into practice in an AI-first engineering environment and work with data engineering and AI-assisted development that creates real business value? Would you like to build your technical skills while contributing to solutions used across Nykredit? Then you might be our new Student Data Engineer in Fund Accounting Products.

As a Student Data Engineer in Fund Accounting Products, you will play an important role in our team, helping us build reports, automate processes and develop the data flows and platforms that support fund valuation, alternatives and fund accounting.

Nykredit is investing heavily in AI, and our team takes an AI-first approach. We actively consider how AI can help us code, test and solve problems more efficiently, while taking responsibility for the quality of the results.

You will also become part of the Nykredit Group, where we offer opportunities and development for those who are curious and eager to learn. Through our student network, Nykredit Youth, you will be invited to professional events and networking opportunities with other students and young colleagues across the Group.

Are you motivated by data engineering and new technologies?

Then you have come to the right place. Your focus will be on reports, data processing, event-driven streaming pipelines and the platforms supporting our business domains.

You will work with technologies such as Python, SQL, Microsoft Fabric, Apache Spark, Azure and Kafka, alongside colleagues using GitHub, Terraform and Grafana for development, deployment and monitoring. These are technologies you will have the opportunity to work with and learn about, not a checklist of things you need to know before applying.

Your tasks will include:

• Developing and improving reports used by the business.

• Preparing, transforming and validating financial data.

• Automating manual tasks using Python and SQL.

• Helping build and test event-driven streaming pipelines and integrations using Kafka.Working with SimCorp Dimension and bringing its data into our Wealth Data Hub.

• Improving monitoring and automation of data flows and operational tasks.

• Exploring how AI can help us modernise legacy code, automate operations and improve data quality.

• Investigating data quality issues and improving existing solutions.

You will start with well-defined tasks and gradually take on more responsibility as you learn, working alongside experienced engineers on real deliveries.

The position is 10–15 hours per week at our headquarters, Nykredit Huset, Sundkrogsgade 25 in Nordhavn, where most of the team is based.

**AI as part of your everyday work

**We work with an AI-first approach: when tackling a task, we actively consider how AI can help us solve it better and more efficiently, while taking responsibility for the quality of the result.

You will get hands-on experience with AI-assisted tools and platforms for coding, testing, documentation and troubleshooting. Together with experienced colleagues, you will explore how AI can help modernise legacy code, automate repetitive work and improve data quality.

We encourage you to experiment and bring your own ideas while learning to understand, review and validate AI-generated output. You do not need experience with specific AI tools before joining us. We will help you get started.

**Are you the one we are looking for?

**We imagine that you:

• are studying Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science or a related field,

• have some experience with Python and SQL from coursework, personal projects or a previous student job,

• enjoy solving problems and working carefully with data,

• are comfortable asking questions and sharing what you learn,

• are curious about AI-assisted development and keen to use it in practice,

• are willing to experiment with AI while questioning, reviewing and understanding the output and code you work with.

We know you are still studying, so we do not expect you to know everything from day one. No financial background is needed, and familiarity with Git, cloud platforms or reporting projects is useful but not required.

What matters most is your curiosity and willingness to learn alongside experienced colleagues. In your application, we would therefore like to hear about a project or assignment you have worked on, how you approached it and what you learned.

Your new team

You will join Fund Accounting Products in Nykredit Wealth Technology, where engineers and specialists work closely with the business.

We are modernising our solutions through the re-implementation of SimCorp Dimension, new SaaS solutions and the replacement of existing in-house systems. You will contribute to both existing solutions and new deliveries, with guidance from experienced colleagues and opportunities to learn how financial requirements translate into working code and reliable data.

We look forward to welcoming you as our new colleague.

**Want to know more?

**You are welcome to contact Development Manager Søren Valther Rasmussen at +45 44 55 51 42 if you have any questions about the position.

If you have questions about the recruitment process, please contact the recruitment team at nytjob@nykredit.dk.

We look forward to receiving your application and CV.

Join Copenhagen Energy Trading as our next Quantitative Researcher - Algorithmic Trading (Short-term Power Markets)

Copenhagen Energy Trading (CET) shapes the future of the energy transition by combining deep market expertise with technical excellence in data, quantitative research and engineering to drive, automate and optimise our trading operations.

We’re a small, elite team based in central Copenhagen specializing in power trading and asset management across Europe and North America. Technology is core to how we operate, powered by exceptional talent and one of Europe’s most advanced automated and analytical trading environments for power markets. But we're not done. We want to push automation and advanced analytics even further, and to do that we need more exceptional people.

The Opportunity

That’s where you come in. We’re looking for an outstanding Quantitative Researcher with a proven track record of building real-time algorithmic trading strategies that operate with high reliability in regulated industries. You'll play a key role in developing strategies for the European short-term power markets.

This isn't a narrow coding or analyst role. You'll have an end-to-end mandate, from prototyping and data engineering to strategy implementation, backtesting and low-latency execution in our algorithmic trading framework. You'll own your projects from idea to P&L, working autonomously alongside a close-knit group of software engineers, quantitative researchers and expert traders.

So, if you feel energized by the intersection of markets, advanced analytics and trading technology and you want to help build something that moves power to where it’s needed the most, then we must talk.

Responsibilities

• Research and model the markets: Analyse energy market dynamics and turn your insights into predictive models that drive profitable trading strategies.

• Own the data: Build and maintain high-quality datasets that combine fundamental and real-time market data.

• Take strategies to production and keep them running: Own the path from research to live trading, shaping the systems, forecasting tools and data pipelines that run our strategies in real time. Once they're live, you'll monitor their performance, handle issues as they come up and make sure they trade reliably day to day.

• Shape the team's direction: Work closely with engineers, quantitative researchers and traders to challenge ideas, share expertise and influence where we take our algorithmic trading next.

• Master the domain: Become a domain expert and understand algorithmic trading architectures and order execution logic in the short-term power markets.

Who are you?

You have:

• Quantitative expertise: A track record of building accurate forecasting models and trading strategies for financial or energy markets, with a rigorous approach to research and validation.

• Software and data skills: Advanced Python skills, and the ability to write clean, efficient, reliable code, backed by solid computer science fundamentals (data structures, algorithms, system design). Strong data skills, from sourcing and cleaning to structuring complex datasets. Some experience with C++ would be a plus.

• Ownership: The ability to work independently and deliver in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong communication: Excellent problem-solving and communication skills with full professional proficiency in English.

• Domain knowledge: A genuine interest in learning about power markets and systems. If you already have that domain knowledge, then that is a big plus.

• Education: An advanced degree in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science or Engineering.

What We Offer

• Growth environment: Be part of a young, ambitious, and expanding tech-driven trading company where talented people are given responsibility and room to grow.

• Exceptional team: Work closely with experienced quantitative researchers, software engineers and power traders.

• Competitive compensation and flexibility: Receive a competitive salary package with benefits and enjoy flexible work arrangements that support your work-life balance.

• Strong culture: Participate in both social and professional events, including team sports, company parties, teambuilding and informal gatherings that strengthen our team spirit.

• Central Copenhagen location: Work from our office in Carlsberg Byen, located in beautifully renovated historic Carlsberg buildings.

About Copenhagen Energy Trading

Copenhagen Energy Trading A/S was founded in 2021 and is part of Copenhagen Energy Group.

We specialize in short-term power trading across Europe and North America. Through technology, data, and market expertise, we develop discretionary and algorithmic trading strategies that help move power to where it is needed most.

Based in Copenhagen, we are building a collaborative, high-performance environment where talented people are trusted with responsibility and given the freedom to make an impact.

How to apply

If this opportunity feels like the right fit for you, we would love to hear from you.

Please apply via LinkedIn and submit your cover letter, CV, and university transcripts as a single PDF. Please note that applications that do not meet these requirements may not be considered.

If you have any questions, please contact Jens Christian Johannsen at jc@copenhagen-energy.com or Anna Schumann at as@copenhagen-energy.com.
